patients.summary: Research scientist in her early 40s with seasonal allergic rhinitis and migraine without aura who joined the practice in 2022. A changing mole on her back in 2024 proved to be a thin stage IA melanoma, treated by wide local excision, now under dermatology surveillance; cleared by occupational health for a research protocol in late 2025.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
40F establishing care. Prior PCP retiring; records requested, not yet here.

She feels well and is here mostly to get set up. Two long-standing issues:
- Seasonal allergies since childhood: sneezing, itchy eyes and congestion, mostly April through June, also bothered by dust at home. Takes cetirizine 10 mg every day, which keeps it tolerable. No asthma, no sinus infections to speak of.
- Migraine without aura since her twenties. Typical pattern for her, never any visual or sensory aura or weakness. A few a month, sometimes clustered around deadlines or poor sleep. Sumatriptan 50 mg at onset aborts most within an hour or two; rarely needs the second dose. Never been on a preventive and doesn't want one.

PMH: as above.
PSH: tonsillectomy age 7; wisdom teeth out at 18.
Meds: cetirizine 10 mg daily; sumatriptan 50 mg prn migraine.
Allergies: penicillin (rash); dust mites.
FHx: mother HTN; father T2DM; maternal grandmother breast cancer at 68. No melanoma or other skin cancer in the family.
Social: PhD research scientist at a biomedical lab. Never smoker. A glass of wine once or twice a week. No drugs. Runs a few mornings a week.
GYN: regular cycles. Last Pap at prior office, she thinks normal, 2019.

ROS: negative except as in HPI.

Exam: well-appearing, NAD. Vitals as recorded. HEENT: TMs clear, turbinates mildly pale, oropharynx clear (tonsils surgically absent). Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement or nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin: scattered small uniform nevi, nothing that catches my eye. Neuro: CN intact, strength and gait normal.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2.

A/P
1. Preventive: fasting CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c (father with diabetes), TSH, and one-time HIV and hep C screening today. Flu shot given. First screening mammogram - order placed, she will schedule for November. Pap due 2024 if the 2019 co-test was normal; will confirm with records. Tdap per records.
2. Allergic rhinitis - stable on cetirizine. Mattress and pillow covers for dust mites discussed.
3. Migraine without aura - well controlled with prn sumatriptan. Reviewed max 2 doses/24h, and to let me know if frequency climbs.

RTC 1 year, sooner prn.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Beth, your bloodwork from Tuesday is all back. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests, thyroid, sugar (A1c) and cholesterol all look healthy, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. It was good to meet you.

documents.title: Allergies
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Pollen season has arrived early, my car is yellow. Quick question: is there any downside to staying on cetirizine every day all year rather than stopping in the winter? I've basically never stopped.

documents.title: RE: Allergies
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No real downside - it is safe long term, and with the dust mite piece being year-round, staying on it makes sense. Some people notice itching for a few days if they stop suddenly, which is another reason not to bother. Saline rinses on the worst pollen days can help too.

orders.reason: changing pigmented lesion of back, urgent

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Mole on back. She noticed it growing starting around the turn of the year, so about 5 months, and over the past 2 weeks it has become itchy. No bleeding. No other spots she is worried about. No personal or family hx of skin cancer.

O: Vitals reviewed. Back: pigmented lesion, roughly a centimeter, with an irregular, notched border and uneven color, brown with a darker black area, part of it slightly raised. Not ulcerated. Remainder of the back and shoulders shows small regular nevi only. No axillary or cervical nodes felt.

A/P: Changing pigmented lesion of the back - fits several of the warning features (asymmetry, border, color, evolution). Needs dermatology eyes and likely a biopsy. Urgent referral placed, asked for an appointment within the month. Talked through what that means without getting ahead of things. She is calm about it, wants to know as soon as anything is known. Photo taken for the chart with her permission.

documents.title: Referral Scheduled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Dermatology accepted the urgent referral. Pt scheduled Fri 6/14 at 9:40 with the dermatology group. Office notes and photo faxed. Pt aware and confirmed.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology consultation, date of service 06/14/2024. Received 06/18/2024.

Reason for referral: changing pigmented lesion on the back.

Ms. Lambert is a 41-year-old research scientist who reports a mole on her back that has enlarged over roughly half a year and has begun to itch in recent weeks. She is worried this could be a skin cancer. She has never had a skin cancer and knows of none in her family.

Past history: seasonal allergic rhinitis; migraine without aura. Surgical: tonsillectomy (age 7), third molar extraction (age 18).
Medications: cetirizine 10 mg daily; sumatriptan 50 mg as needed.
Allergies: penicillin (rash); dust mites.
Social: never smoker; alcohol 1-2 drinks weekly; biomedical research scientist.

Examination: full skin examination performed. On the back there is a 1.2 cm pigmented lesion with irregular borders and variegated pigment ranging from brown to black, with a slightly raised nodular component. The remainder of the skin examination, including scalp, nails and mucosa, is unremarkable. No cervical, axillary or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

Impression: pigmented lesion of the back, clinically suspicious for melanoma.

Plan: After consent, excisional biopsy performed today with 2 mm margins, elliptical excision, layered closure. Specimen sent for histopathology, oriented. Wound care reviewed. Sutures out in 2 weeks. We will contact her with results and send a copy to you.

Thank you for this referral.

conditions.label: Malignant melanoma of other part of trunk
conditions.note: back; superficial spreading, Breslow 0.6 mm, non-ulcerated, pT1a

reports.text:
Specimen: skin, back, excisional biopsy, oriented with suture at 12 o'clock.
Gross: an ellipse of skin measuring 2.0 x 1.4 cm, excised to a depth of 0.6 cm, bearing a variegated brown-black lesion measuring 1.2 cm in greatest dimension. Inked, serially sectioned and entirely submitted.
Microscopic: an asymmetric, poorly circumscribed proliferation of atypical melanocytes with pagetoid spread and confluent junctional nests, with an invasive dermal component in the area corresponding to the raised portion.
Synoptic: histologic type superficial spreading melanoma. Maximum tumor (Breslow) thickness 0.6 mm. Ulceration not identified. Dermal mitotic rate less than 1 per mm2. Microsatellites not identified. Lymphovascular invasion not identified. Perineural invasion not identified. Peripheral margins negative for invasive and in situ melanoma, closest 1 mm. Deep margin negative. Pathologic stage (AJCC 8th): pT1a.
reports.conclusion: Skin, back, excision: invasive melanoma, superficial spreading type, Breslow thickness 0.6 mm, non-ulcerated, mitoses less than 1/mm2, margins negative (closest 1 mm). pT1a.

documents.title: Outside Pathology Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Path from dermatology's 6/14 biopsy came in this morning: superficial spreading melanoma, 0.6 mm, no ulceration, <1 mitosis/mm2, margins clear but narrow, pT1a. Dermatology plans wide excision. Added melanoma to problem list. Will call her now - want her to hear it from one of us before the derm office's call if possible.

documents.title: Pathology Results Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt. Dermatology had reached her yesterday evening, so she knew the word melanoma but had questions. Went over the report in plain terms: thin (0.6 mm), not ulcerated, very low mitotic rate, which puts it in the earliest invasive category with an excellent outlook. Next step is a wider excision with 1 cm margins; for this thickness a lymph node biopsy and scans are not usually recommended, and dermatology will confirm. She asked good questions - as she put it, she reads papers for a living, she just never expected to read about herself. She has the WLE booked for 7/12. Offered a visit anytime to talk it through; she'll reach out after the surgery.

events.reason: wide local excision, melanoma of back

documents.title: Wide Local Excision
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Dermatologic surgery procedure note. Date of procedure 07/12/2024. Received 07/16/2024.

Preoperative and postoperative diagnosis: invasive melanoma of the back, Breslow 0.6 mm, non-ulcerated, pT1a, status post excisional biopsy 06/14/2024.

Procedure: wide local excision with 1 cm margins measured from the biopsy scar, with intermediate layered closure.

Allergies: penicillin (rash). Medications reviewed.

After informed consent and time-out, the area was marked with 1 cm margins around the healing biopsy scar and anesthetized with lidocaine 1% with epinephrine. Excision was carried to the level of the fascia. Specimen oriented and sent for pathology. Hemostasis with electrocautery. Wound closed in layers with absorbable deep sutures and nylon to the skin. Estimated blood loss minimal. No complications; the patient tolerated it well.

Discussion: sentinel lymph node biopsy and staging imaging are not indicated for a T1a melanoma without clinical nodal disease; reviewed with the patient.

Aftercare: keep dry 48 hours, then gentle washing. Avoid heavy lifting and strenuous upper-body exercise for 2 weeks. Suture removal in 14 days in our office. Acetaminophen for discomfort.

reports.text:
Specimen: skin and subcutaneous tissue, back, wide local excision, oriented.
Gross: an ellipse of skin measuring 6.0 x 3.4 cm with subcutaneous tissue to a depth of 1.5 cm, bearing a 2.0 cm healing linear scar. Margins inked; scar region entirely submitted, margins representatively submitted.
Microscopic: dermal scar with granulation tissue and foreign body giant cell reaction consistent with prior biopsy site. No residual in situ or invasive melanoma identified. All margins free.
reports.conclusion: Skin, back, wide local excision: healing biopsy site; no residual melanoma. Margins negative.

documents.title: Dermatology Treatment Summary
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I am writing to update you on our mutual patient Ms. Beth Lambert. She underwent wide local excision with 1 cm margins on 07/12/2024 for a superficial spreading melanoma of the back (Breslow 0.6 mm, non-ulcerated, mitotic rate <1/mm2). Final pathology shows no residual melanoma with clear margins. Her final stage is IA (pT1a, clinically node-negative).

No further treatment is required. We will see her every 6 months for full skin and lymph node examination. She has been counseled on monthly self skin examination, broad-spectrum sunscreen and protective clothing, and to call us for any new or changing lesion or a lump in the armpits or neck.

Allergies on file: penicillin (rash), dust mites.

With thanks,
Dermatology

documents.title: Outside Records Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: WLE path clear, stage IA. Derm surveillance q6 months. Problem list updated with stage. Nothing for us to do beyond keeping an eye on the scar and nodes at her physical.

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi - just wanted to say thank you for calling me in June when the biopsy came back, it helped a lot. Dermatology says the excision was clear. The incision is sore but healing, stitches come out next week. I'll see you at my physical in the fall.

documents.title: RE: Update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That is the best possible news, Beth - I'm so glad. Take it easy on the back until dermatology clears you. See you this fall, and message anytime before then.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based ThinPrep. Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV (cobas): not detected.
reports.conclusion: NILM. High-risk HPV not detected. Routine co-testing in 5 years.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 42 y/o F.

Since last year: melanoma of the back, found in May, biopsied 6/14 (superficial spreading, 0.6 mm, non-ulcerated, pT1a) and widely excised 7/12 with clear margins - stage IA. Derm following q6mo, first surveillance visit January. She's doing well emotionally, a rough couple of weeks in June. Now wears a hat and sunscreen on weekends outdoors.
Migraine: same pattern, 2 to 3 a month, sumatriptan effective. Rhinitis fine on cetirizine.

Meds: cetirizine 10 mg daily; sumatriptan 50 mg prn.
Allergies: PCN - rash; dust mites.
FHx: unchanged.
Social: never smoker, 1-2 drinks/wk.

Exam: well, NAD. HEENT nl. Neck, supraclavicular and axillary nodes negative. CV RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft. Back: well-healed linear excision scar, flat, no pigment or nodularity along it. Visual skin survey otherwise unremarkable. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal appearing, Pap with HPV obtained. Neuro nonfocal.

PHQ-2 1.

A/P
- Hx melanoma stage IA, s/p WLE: no evidence of recurrence on my exam. Keep derm schedule.
- Health maintenance: Pap/HPV today. CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c. Flu and COVID given. Mammogram due November - ordered. Colon screening starts at 45.
- Migraine and rhinitis: stable, continue.

Return 1 yr.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Beth, everything from last week is normal: blood count, chemistries, A1c and cholesterol, and your Pap with the HPV test was negative. With a normal co-test you won't need another Pap for 5 years.

reports.text: Bilateral screening digital mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison 11/14/2023 and 11/08/2022. Breast composition: scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious masses, calcifications or areas of distortion. No change from priors.

documents.title: Mammogram Result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Beth, mammogram normal, no change from prior years. Next due next November.

documents.title: Dermatology Surveillance Visit
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Dermatology follow-up, date of service 01/17/2025. Received 01/21/2025.

Ms. Lambert returns six months after wide local excision of a stage IA melanoma of the back (pT1a, Breslow 0.6 mm). She reports no new or changing spots and no lumps.

Allergies: penicillin (rash); dust mites. Medications: cetirizine, sumatriptan as needed.

Full skin examination: the excision scar on the back is well healed, flat and without pigment, nodularity or satellite lesions. No new atypical or suspicious lesions elsewhere. Cervical, axillary and inguinal nodes not palpable.

Assessment: history of melanoma, no evidence of recurrence.

Plan: continue monthly self-examination and sun protection. Return in 6 months for full skin examination.

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning - the pharmacy says I'm out of refills on both the cetirizine and the sumatriptan. Same doses as always. Thank you!

documents.title: RE: Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Beth, the doctor approved both: cetirizine 10 mg daily, 90 days with 3 refills, and sumatriptan 50 mg, 9 tablets with 5 refills. They should be ready later today.

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, she's at her office, consented, ID verified.

Her usual spring allergies have come on hard the last 10 days with the warm stretch: sneezing, runny nose, itchy watery eyes, worse after her lunchtime walks. Still taking cetirizine daily. No fever, facial pain, wheeze or shortness of breath. Not sick otherwise.

On video: comfortable, mild conjunctival injection, speaking full sentences, no distress.

A/P: seasonal allergic rhinitis, typical flare at peak tree pollen. Keep the cetirizine. Shower and change after time outside, windows closed, saline rinse twice a day, take the cetirizine in the evening so it covers the morning peak. Dust mite covers already in place. She'll message if not settling by mid-May.

documents.author: PCP

- Migraine w/o aura: unchanged, a few a month, sumatriptan works. Uses well under the monthly supply.

PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 2.

Next physical fall 2026.

Occupational Health Service
